(i) a robot can autonomously scan a scene to reconstruct it in a way that it can be analyzed for object detection and segmentation and (ii) the analysis of the reconstructed scene can guide the robot to acquire additional data to improve the quality of the analysis.
we develop a novel framework to enable autonomous scanning for coupled scene reconstruction, object analysis, and proactive object-wise data acquisition.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a framework and algorithms for autoscanning, object reconstruction, and object-level analysis.

the design and development of an integrated framework that combines the following components: 1) an object-level scene representation, 2) an autoscanning algorithm that drives the robot to acquire the scene in an object-aware manner, 3) a scene analysis algorithm that progressively improves the object-level scene understanding, 4) an object-level validation algorithm that validates the object-level scene analysis and drives the robot to collect more data if needed, and 5) a robot control system that executes the above components
the following three problems: (1) How to reconstruct a 3D scene in an object-wise fashion, (2) How to analyze the scene at the required level and (3) How to guide a robot for the scene acquisition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed framework enables a robot to autonomously scan and analyze indoor scenes in a proactive manner.
we propose an autoscanning and analysis framework that is guided by an object-centric scene analysis, which in turn is improved by the autoscanning process.
we develop a novel framework for autoscanning of indoor scenes, which is guided and improved by object analysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we develop a novel framework for autonomous scene reconstruction coupled with scene analysis, and we demonstrate it with a real-world implementation of a robotic scanning system.

, we develop a framework for autoscanning and scene reconstruction, where the robot is driven to acquire data for the reconstruction and analysis, and the analysis, in turn, drives the robot to acquire more data for the reconstruction.
we develop an autonomous system for detailed scene acquisition coupled with scene analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the object-centric scene analysis can be effectively used for proactive object-wise validation of scene reconstruction.
the analysis and reconstruction are not only coupled, but also mutually benefit from each other.
, by exploiting the object-centric scene analysis, we can achieve a more efficient scene reconstruction with fewer data points.
